newsitem.title: CHINA: China's wheat, corn prices seen weak in July.
newsitem.headline: China's wheat, corn prices seen weak in July.

text.p: China's grain and edible oil prices were expected to remain weak in July because of oversupply, the Futures Herald said in its Friday edition received here on Monday.
China's domestic wheat prices were expected to fluctuate at relatively low levels in July, the newspaper said, quoting the Zhengzhou Commodity Exchange.
Supply of wheat still exceeded demand with trading activity subdued in June, it said. The average national wheat price stood at 1,516 yuan ($182.6) per tonne in June, down from 1,608 yuan in May.
Domestic corn prices were likely to remain sluggish in July because current bearish international prices were unfavourable for China's exports, thus pushing up supply, it said.
The average national corn price stood at 1,067 yuan per tonne in June, down from 1,081 yuan in May, it said.

China's average national price of long-grain rice was 1,855 yuan in June, down from 1,914 yuan in May, it said. The price of round-grain rice was 2,168 yuan in June, up from 2,165 yuan in May, it said.

The average national price of soybeans was 3,176 yuan per tonne in June, down from 3,183 yuan in May, it said. A fall in soybean prices was mainly triggered by a rise in imports and slack consumption in the first half.

The average price of peanut oil was 9,857 yuan per tonne in June, down from 9,867 yuan in May, rapeseed oil at 7,383 yuan per tonne, down from 7,486 yuan and soybean oil at 7,245 yuan, down from 7,404 yuan, it said.
